root_cause: leaveGroupImpl's purge called removeGroupFromStorage = groupStorage.deleteGroup, which deletes only the overlay record (few-groups-meta). Nothing ever called marmotClient.groups.destroy for a left or abandoned group, so its MLS state (keys, history, snapshots) stayed in few-groups-state forever. It was loaded into marmot's cache at every startup, and collectBackupPayload exported every state key, so the keys also rode along in every relay backup and were restored on other devices.
fix: Design Part 1. New leftGroupTombstones.ts: an idb-keyval store few-left-groups/tombstones holding {groupId, leftAt}, with put, delete, list (malformed rows ignored), listLeftGroupIds and clearAll. leaveGroupImpl writes the tombstone before removeGroupFromStorage; a failed write is warned and the purge still runs. When a kind-9 announcement is in flight, the destroy is chained without being awaited: settledOrTimeout(send, LEAVE_DESTROY_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000) → destroyGroupState → deleteLeftGroupTombstone, so purge and navigation stay immediate. With no send (abandon, no MLS group, no identity) it runs inline before reloadGroups. A failed destroy keeps the tombstone. destroyGroupState is wired in MarmotContext to welcomeSubscription.destroyLeftGroupState. That function runs under withGroupJoinLock(id): overlay present → 'rejoined', nothing destroyed; no MLS state → 'absent'; otherwise groups.destroy(id), which is local-only. This also keeps a late leave-chain destroy from removing a group that was re-joined within the 5 s. sweepLeftGroups runs in loadGroupsAndReconcileInvitations after loadAll and before dropInvitationsForJoinedGroups. It only looks at tombstoned groups and drops each tombstone after destroyLeftGroupState; on a failure it keeps the tombstone and never blocks startup. joinIdempotent's orphan branch deletes the tombstone after its destroy. collectBackupPayload exports state only for overlay group ids that are not tombstoned. clearAllGroupData clears the tombstones. No new publishes. Interpretation (VQ-2): for tombstone + overlay, the sweep never destroys MLS state but does drop the stale tombstone. Otherwise a crash mid-leave would exclude a live group from backups forever.
tests_added: leaveGroupImpl.test.ts (+11, all failed pre-fix): the tombstone is written before the overlay delete. Normal leave resolves while the send is pending and never destroys before it settles. The destroy then the tombstone delete run after the send resolves, after it rejects, and only after the 5 s timeout (fake timers, nothing at 4999 ms). Abandon and no-mlsGroup destroy inline (order put → removeOverlay → destroy → deleteTombstone → reload). A failing inline or deferred destroy keeps the tombstone and does not throw. A failing tombstone write never skips the purge or the destroy. A purge failure leaves the tombstone for the sweep. Mutation-driven: assertions on the kind-13 content and the warn message.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Design Part 1 says the leave chain calls groups.destroy(id) directly. Taken literally, it races a re-join inside the 5 s window: joinIdempotent's orphan destroy, then a fresh join, then the late leave destroy wipes the new group. A destroy that runs only after the send resolves could also run before the overlay was deleted. The chained destroy therefore goes through a lock-guarded, overlay-checking destroyLeftGroupState, scheduled after the purge. VQ-2's 'tombstone + overlay → untouched' did not say what happens to the tombstone. Keeping it would exclude a live group's state from backups forever.
retrospective.surprised_by: docs/behavior/groups.md had three stale 'no admin removal of a confirmed member' claims (§4.4, §8, §12), not only the one in §12 the report named. §4.4's 'cancel is a no-op once confirmed' guard also no longer exists: cancelInvitationImpl now gates on tree membership only.

findings: F2 (Codex medium): the tombstone was dropped only in joinIdempotent's orphan branch. Sequence: destroy succeeds, tombstone delete fails, then a re-accept finds groups.has false and skips that branch. The rejoined group kept a stale tombstone and was excluded from the backup until the next start.
Docs: §7 said the keys are erased after the announcement is 'sent' (it is after sent, failed or 5 s); the backup wording did not hold in the double-failure case.
remediation_round_1.code: welcomeSubscription.ts joinIdempotent: the orphan-branch delete was replaced by dropLeftGroupTombstoneAfterJoin(groupId). It runs under the join lock after every successful join: the fresh join after joinAndPersist, and the already-joined return. A delete failure is warned and does not fail the accept. A failed join keeps the tombstone.
remediation_round_1.docs: groups.md §7: keys are erased once sending the announcement has finished (sent or failed) or after about 5 s. Interrupted or failed deletion completes at next start. Guarantee reworded to 'beyond the next start'. New 'Rejoining' bullet: a rejoined group is backed up again; if the device also fails to record the rejoin, it stays out of the backup until the next start. backup-and-recovery.md §3 has the same caveat.
remediation_round_1.tests_added: leftGroupStatePurge.test.ts +3. (1) Leave destroy ok and tombstone delete failed, then re-accept with groups.has false: tombstone gone and collectBackupPayload contains the group's state. (2) Already-joined accept drops a stale tombstone. (3) Failed join keeps the tombstone. Cases 1 and 2 fail on the round-0 code by construction (no orphan branch reached).
